description:
Follow-up to ISS-048, which shipped the pattern-key mechanism while leaving the threshold at the inherited Jaccard 0.40 / sharedCount 2. Asked "what would you suggest for the threshold ISS-048 will gate on", so it was measured rather than guessed.

METHOD: 18 labelled positive pairs (the same pattern phrased as a session agent would on different days, drawn from the real ACTIVE.md patterns and PERSONA themes) against 200 negatives.

FIRST ANSWER WAS WRONG, AND THE TEST SUITE CAUGHT IT. The initial evaluation used only cross-group negatives — patterns that are semantically far apart. It reported 100% precision at every threshold and recommended overlap 0.50 / sharedCount 2. Applying that broke an existing test: reinforcePattern("First pattern reinforced more") and ("Second pattern reinforced less") collapsed into one pattern, sharing {pattern, reinforced} = 2 of a 4-word smaller set = exactly 0.50. The labelled set had no negatives of that shape, so the evaluation could not have caught it. The repo's own tests did.

RE-MEASURED with 8 ADVERSARIAL negatives added — same structure, discriminating word swapped ("prefers concise responses" / "prefers verbose responses", "verifies claims against primary sources" / "...secondary sources"). Precision collapses across the board; no setting of either metric reaches both good recall and good precision. Like-for-like at equal 67% recall:

  jaccard 0.40 / 2  (previous) : precision 71%, 5 of 8 adversarial pairs wrongly merged
  overlap 0.50 / 3  (chosen)   : precision 86%, 2 of 8 adversarial pairs wrongly merged

TWO REASONS FOR THE CHANGE:

1. METRIC. Jaccard divides by the union, so unequal-length keys are structurally capped — "frames problems by root cause" against "starts from root cause before proposing fixes" shares 2 content words of a 7-word union and can never exceed 0.29 however right the match is. Agents do not write keys at a consistent length, so the penalty fires constantly. Overlap (shared / smaller set) removes it: full containment scores 1.

2. sharedCount 3, NOT the ratio. Across overlap 0.30-0.60 the ratio barely moves the numbers; raising sharedCount from 2 to 3 lifts precision 70% -> 86% and cuts adversarial merges from 7 to 2. Requiring three shared content words is what rejects "prefers concise responses" / "prefers verbose responses", which share only two.

STATED HONESTLY: precision is 86%, not 100%. Roughly one merge in seven is expected wrong, and the residual failures are semantic opposites that no bag-of-words metric can separate — both keys carry the same words and differ by one. This is tolerable ONLY because a merge does not silently become a lesson: getLessonCandidates surfaces candidates for zug_create_lesson to promote, so a bad merge is visible at promotion rather than baked in. The code comment says not to reuse this gate anywhere lacking that review step.

PROVISIONAL. Derived from hand-authored phrasings because the pattern-key feature has no production data — there are currently zero real keys. Re-derive once a few dozen accumulate; the dashboard's Recurrence panel runs this sweep interactively and its slider now controls overlap.

CHANGES: MATCH_THRESHOLD and overlapSimilarity exported from src/storage.ts, findBestMatch and autoReinforceSession's within-session dedup switched to it; mirrored in web/lib/zug-cluster.ts; the shared fixture regenerated to carry overlap alongside jaccard so both implementations stay pinned; Recurrence slider relabelled. Jaccard is retained and still fixture-pinned, since getLessonCandidates uses its sharedCount for lesson dedup.

VERIFIED: root 265/265, web 104/104, both typechecks clean, and the end-to-end runEndSession path still promotes a pattern across three different phrasings to a lesson candidate.
title: Reinforcement matching: overlap coefficient at 0.50/3, replacing Jaccard 0.40/2
